chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Yemen.
Yemen is a historic mountainous and cultural country in the Middle East.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Yemen?
Yemen is in West Asia in the southern part of the Arabian Peninsula.
It is next to Saudi Arabia and Oman.
It also touches the Red Sea and the Arabian Sea.
It has mountains, deserts, and a long coastline.
What is the capital city of Yemen?
The capital city is Sanaa.
Sanaa is a very old city.
It has unique buildings, mosques, and bazaars, markets.
It is high in the mountains and has cooler weather.
Other cities include Aden, a port city on the sea.
Taiz, a cultural and historic city.
Al -Hudaida on the Red Sea coast.
Mukalla in the east by the Arabian Sea.
How many people live in Yemen?
About 30 million people live in Yemen.
Most people live in cities, mountain villages, or farming areas.
Life is often traditional and family -based.
What language do people speak in Yemen?
The official language is Arabic.
People speak Yemeni Arabic, which has many accents.
Some people also speak English, especially in cities or schools.
In some areas, people speak ancient South Arabian languages.
What is the weather like in Yemen?
Yemen has different climates.
The coast is hot and humid.
The mountains are cooler and dry.
The desert is very hot and dry.
Rain is rare, but the mountains get more rain than the lowlands.
What does Yemen look like?
Yemen has tall mountains and deep valleys, deserts and green farms, old villages built on hills, long coastlines with beaches, the island of Sokotra, famous for unique trees and animals.
Yemen has many UNESCO World Heritage sites.
What animals live in Yemen?
In Yemen, you can find camels, donkeys, goats and sheep, foxes, wolves and baboons in the mountains, birds like eagles, falcons and doves.
On Sokotra Island, strange animals and plants not found anywhere else in the world.
What do people eat in Yemen?
Yemeni food is spiced, simple and home -cooked.
People eat bread called kubes or malawa, rice, lentils and beans, chicken, lamb and sometimes fish, tomatoes, onions and potatoes.
Popular dishes, salta, a hot stew with meat, vegetables and hulba, fenugreek foam.
Fasa, shredded meat stew served hot in a stone bowl.
Bentalsan, a sweet layered bread with honey and butter.
Shafoot, cold bread with yogurt and herbs eaten in summer.
Meals are often eaten together on the floor with the right hand.
What do people drink in Yemen?
People drink water and black tea with mint or milk.
Coffee, Yemen is one of the birth places of coffee.
Cheshire, a hot drink made from coffee, husks and ginger.
Fresh juices like mango or lemon.
In Yemen, people also chew cot, a local plant in the afternoon to relax and socialize.
What is life like in Yemen?
Life in Yemen is often traditional, family centered and community based.
People enjoy spending time with family, cooking and eating together.
Telling stories, poetry and music.
Walking in the village or shopping in markets.
Celebrating with dances and songs.
What are some holidays and traditions?
Eid al -Fitr, end of Ramadan.
Eid al -Adha, the feast of sacrifice.
National Unity Day, May 22nd.
Wedding celebrations with drums, dances and henna.
Religious festivals, special prayers and family meals.
People wear traditional clothes like white robes, scarves and jambias.
Curved knives worn by men.
Some fun facts about Yemen.
Yemen was once called Arabia Felix, meaning Happy Arabia.
The city of Shabbam is called the Manhattan of the Desert.
Sanaa has buildings that are over 1,000 years old.
The dragon blood tree grows only on Sokotra Island.
The Yemeni flag is red, white and black.
Now you know many things about Yemen.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the mountains, traditions and food well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emili.
